headline: José Luis Castro: No country can treat its way out of chronic respiratory diseases
dek: The WHO Special Envoy said he co-authored an eClinicalMedicine article proposing a four-level prevention framework for chronic inflammatory airways diseases.
body:
José Luis Castro, WHO Director-General's Special Envoy for Chronic Respiratory Diseases, wrote on LinkedIn that "no country can treat its way out of the growing burden of chronic respiratory diseases".

He said he co-authored an article published on the day of his post in eClinicalMedicine – The Lancet Discovery Science, part of The Lancet Group of journals. According to Castro, the publication emerged from the EUFOREA Respiratory Summit, which was convened at his suggestion in London in June 2026.

The article proposes a four-level prevention framework for chronic inflammatory airways diseases. Castro said it shifts the emphasis from reactive treatment to proactive, patient-centred care. The article is open access.

In his post, Castro said he sees prevention, stronger primary healthcare and equitable access to diagnostics and essential medicines as fundamental to reducing the global burden of these diseases. He described the 2025 World Health Assembly resolution on integrated lung health as providing important political momentum, adding that scientific evidence and political commitments must now be translated into action.

Castro thanked EUFOREA, Professor Peter Hellings, Xander Bertels and all co-authors.
key_quote: No country can treat its way out of the growing burden of chronic respiratory diseases.
